newsitem.title: USA: CBOT May soybeans surge to contract high on Sparks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT May soybeans surge to contract high on Sparks.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply higher on Wednesday and a contract high was notched in the May after Sparks Companies executive Willard Sparks said he expected gains in soybean prices, traders said.

"I guess the world was startled back into the reality that we need to ration supply through higher prices," said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter in Chicago. "Willard Sparks was telling the world that soybeans (are tight) and there were rumors about Chinese purchases again."
In an interview with Reuters on Tuesday, Sparks said CBOT soybeans were set to rise sharply, notably old crop months.

Sparks said tight U.S. soybean supplies would push July futures to $9.00 per bushel, possibly up to $9.75. The U.S. Agriculture Department earlier this month put soybean ending stocks at a tight 125 million bushels.
The new contract high for the May is $8.92 per bushel, eclipsing the previous high of $8.88-1/2 set on April 3 and the highest level for a spot contract since 1988.
Soybeans ended 22 to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher with July up 21-1/4 at $8.87.
Sparks' comments fueled ongoing concerns that tight U.S. soybean supplies would not last through the summer unless prices rose enough to ration demand.

Talk China was again looking to buy U.S. soybeans compounded those concerns, as did ideas Thursday's USDA export sales figure would be high. U.S. exporters could not confirm additional sales to China.

Trade sources estimated Thursday's USDA export report would show between 350,000 and 450,000 tonnes of soybeans sold. But some floor sources suggested the range of guesses was wider. They cited conflicting ideas on how many cargoes of U.S. soybeans have been sold to China.

Technically, the July contract was giving off bullish signals. Some trade sources had warned a bearish "head and shoulders" formation was developing but Wednesday's sharp gains change the look on the charts to a bullish "flag" formation, technical traders said.

On the day, funds bought at least 14 million bushels of soybeans, keying off the chart signals, floor sources said. Prudential Securities bought five million bushels July, Dean Witter bought three million July and Refco Inc bought and sold three million July, pit sources said.

Spreads were again active as the July/November spread gained 14-1/4 cents per bushel to close at $1.89-1/2, premium July. The spread had traded at $1.92, the widest since the July and November 1997 contracts were listed.
Sparks on Tuesday projected the spread would widen to $2.00 to $2.50, premium July.
Term Commodities spread 2.5 million bushels July/November at $1.85, premium July, Prudential Securities spread one million July/November at $1.84 to $1.87.
In options trade, FIMAT Futures bought 500 November $7.00 puts at 44 to 43-1/4 cents.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 90,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 71,645.
